title: Telemetry stewardship and metric SLA notes
content:
Purpose
This doc captures a proposal and working notes for establishing telemetry stewardship (who owns which metrics/traces), metric SLAs, dashboard lifecycle rules, and practical tracing sampling guidance for inference services. Goal: make our observable surface reliable and sustainable while keeping on-call noise low and maintaining actionable dashboards for SREs, serving/runtime engineers, and product owners.

Summary of proposals (high-level)
- Metric stewardship: assign a single owner (team + person) per metric family and per dashboard. Owners are responsible for semantics, alerts, and breaking changes.
- Metric SLA: each critical metric has an SLA (availability and freshness) and an associated alert policy. Non-critical metrics move to a best-effort tier with retention/pruning rules.
- Dashboard lifecycle: introduce "staging -> active -> archived" lifecycle and quarterly pruning. Dashboards without an owner or without views in 90 days move to archived.
- Tracing sampling budgets: tokenized-inference traces sampled at different rates depending on route tier (prod-critical 10%, prod-noncritical 1%, canaries 100%) plus adaptive sampling for errors.

Owner & steward model
- Stewardship table (examples to be converted to a quick CSV):
  - inference/request_latency_ms (p50/p95/p99): owner=eng-serving-runtime, steward=Marcus Chen.
  - inference/kvcache_hit_ratio: owner=eng-serving-runtime, steward=Lina Gomez.
  - api/error_rate_5m: owner=product-hosted-api, steward=Priya Nair.
- Owners must: document meaning, units, histogram vs gauge decision, expected cardinality, and approved alerts in the metric contract (see linked Confluence).
- Change process: any renaming/removal must go through an issue with tag "telemetry-change", include migration plan and aliasing window (>=14 days).

Metric SLA & alerting guidance
- SLO tiers: Critical (customer-visible latency, availability), Important (inference quality regressions, backend error spikes), Insight (cost, infra-level metrics).
- Example SLA for request latency metrics:
  - Availability SLA: metric scrape success >= 99.9% across region per day.
  - Freshness SLA: max age of latest datapoint <= 2 minutes for high-traffic routes.
  - Alert thresholds: create 3-tier alerts: warn (p95 > target * 1.1 for 5m), high (p95 > target * 1.3 for 3m), page (p99 > target * 1.5 and concurrent errors > 1% for 1m).
- Alert fatigue controls: use alert grouping by route/model, automatic dedup windows, and suppression for known maintenance windows.

Tracing conventions and contract
- Span naming: use dot-separated path: service.operation.stage (e.g., serving.decode.kvcache_lookup). Keep names <= 64 chars.
- Tags/attributes: must include: request_id, route, model_version, customer_tier, sequence_length_bucket. Avoid high-cardinality free-text tags.
- Span boundaries: instrument at these boundaries: ingress parsing, routing/selection, model token generation loop, cache lookup/set, compile/kernel selection, network send/receive to external providers.
- Error spans: set span.status = ERROR and add attribute error.kind and error.message (truncated).
- Sampling:
  - Default base sample: 0.5% (prod-noncritical).
  - Prod-critical routes: 10% base.
  - For any error (HTTP 5xx, internal exception), force-sample the trace and keep for min 7 days for regression investigations.
  - Adaptive sampling: if tail latency anomaly detected, temporarily increase sampling for impacted routes (see ticket OBS-412).

PromQL/Query examples (to be copied to dashboards)
- p95 request latency (ms) for route "chat":
  - histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(inference_request_latency_bucket{route=\"chat\"}[5m])) by (le)) * 1000
- kv cache hit rate:
  - sum(rate(inference_kvcache_hit_total[5m])) / sum(rate(inference_kvcache_lookup_total[5m]))
- error rate by model version (5m):
  - sum(rate(inference_errors_total[5m])) by (model_version) / sum(rate(inference_requests_total[5m])) by (model_version)

Dashboard layout & pruning rules
- Per-service dashboard template sections (top to bottom):
  1) Health overview (availability, error rate, synthetic canary)
  2) Latency slices (p50/p95/p99, heatmap for token latency)
  3) Throughput & batching (requests/s, tokens/s, batch size histogram)
  4) Cost surface (GPU utilization, bytes moved, cache savings estimate)
  5) Traces & recent error examples (links to trace view)
  6) Ownership & runbook link
- Pruning policy:
  - Quarterly dashboard audit (obs-triage team) -> owner notified. If owner does not respond in 14 days, dashboard moves to archived state. Archived dashboards kept for 1 year then deleted.
  - Metrics referenced on <=1 active dashboard and low cardinality (<=50 series) get considered for migration to aggregated metrics or removal.

Instrumentation checklist (for devs shipping metrics/traces)
- Write a short metric contract: name, unit, help text, expected labels and cardinality, alerting rationale.
- Add tests: ensure metric is emitted in unit/integration tests and exported in local e2e with sampling disabled.
- Add dashboard stub in staging that references the new metric (even if temporary).
- Add an entry to telemetry-change backlog for future review.

Synthetic canaries and runbooks
- Canary design: lightweight synthetic that runs a short chat prompt through the stack and validates: successful response, latency target, and no error spans. Run every 60s in each region.
- Canary alerting: failing 3 consecutive canary runs -> create a P0 if customer-facing canary returns incorrect output or >2x latency SLO.
- Runbook quick steps: check recent deployments, trace sample for request_id from canary, check GPU / queue depth, fall back routes if applicable.

Open questions / TODOs
- Decide exact retention window for sampled error traces: 7d vs 30d (cost tradeoff).
- Define concrete sampling knobs per customer tier and make runtime-configurable. (Owner: Omar Ruiz, ticket INFRA-1985)
- Build a small "telemetry-lint" tool to validate contracts in PRs. POC in instrumentation repo.

Notes to self / meeting fragments:
- "we should avoid creating dozens of tiny dashboards per experiment" — want standardized templates + quicknotes for experimenters.
- Push on training for product teams: how to be metric stewards (template + office hours).

References and related tickets:
- OBS-412: telemetry budgeting and adaptive sampling (linked above)
- INFRA-1985: runtime sampling toggles

Appendix: example alert rule (pseudo-YAML)
- name: inference-high-p95-latency
  expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(inference_request_latency_bucket{route=\"*\"}[5m])) by (le, route)) > (route_target_seconds * 1.3)
  for: 3m
  labels: {severity: "high", team: "eng-serving-runtime"}
  annotations: {summary: "High p95 latency for {{ $labels.route }}"}

End of doc.

-- Aisha (notes, draft)
